ribbon.aria: The kinds of groups that run on Initiative

invited.title: Somebody added you. Now what?
invited.description: Most people arrive because their group already lives here and somebody sent a link. There's nothing to set up, and you don't need to know what a Kanban board is. If you've ever written a shopping list, you're overqualified.
invited.step1Title: Open the link you were sent
invited.step1Body: It makes your account and drops you into your group. Already have one? It just adds the community to it.
invited.step2Body: Everything's already there. Click things. Open menus. Drag stuff about.
invited.step3Body: Deleted something? It's in the Trash, sulking. Moved a task somewhere daft? Move it back. Nobody saw.

tools.title: Learn one tool, know the rest
tools.description: Everything inside a community is a tool. They're shared the same way, tagged the same way, commented on the same way — so the second one feels familiar before you've opened it.
tools.projects: Boards, lists and a calendar of the same tasks. Due dates, subtasks, and the tasks that are secretly three tasks wearing a coat.
tools.documents: Pages, spreadsheets and whiteboards, edited together, with the conversation about them sitting right on them.
tools.queues: Whose turn it is to email the council. Nobody's turn. It's always nobody's turn. Put it in a queue.
tools.counterGroups: Tally the things you'd otherwise count on your fingers. Tickets sold, cakes promised, chairs still missing.
tools.calendars: Rehearsals, match days, the AGM. With reminders, so the reminder isn't you.
tools.dashboards: One screen with the numbers on it, readable from the far end of a draughty hall.
tools.wikis: What the group knows, rather than what it's doing. The thing somebody explained in a message once, written down where the next person will actually find it.
tools.posts: Announcements that stay put, instead of scrolling away under forty replies.
tools.galleries: Photos from the day, kept with the day, not in six people's camera rolls.

download.title: Get the app
download.description: It runs in a browser, and using it that way forever is a completely respectable life choice. But it can also have its own icon, its own window, and — on Android — notifications that arrive while you aren't looking.
download.androidNote: Or let <1>Obtainium</1> keep it updated for you.
download.iosNote: Share button, then Add to Home Screen. Same app, no store.
download.desktopNote: The install icon at the right-hand end of the address bar. Or don't, and use the tab. Also fine.
